objects.description: Bi-directional iterator over set bit positions of a roaring::Roaring bitmap. Supports forward/backward iteration, comparison, and seeking to the first value >= a target. Instances are typically created via Roaring::begin() and compared to Roaring::end().

Context object to accelerate repeated add/contains operations on a single Roaring bitmap with the *Bulk APIs. Must be default-constructed and used with one bitmap only; any non-bulk modification of that bitmap invalidates associated contexts.

C++ wrapper for a Roaring bitmap with value semantics and rich API: construction from arrays or initializer lists, set operations, serialization (portable and native), rank/select, iterators, copy-on-write, run optimization, and frozen views. Manages an embedded C roaring_bitmap_t and its lifetime.

Bidirectional iterator over set bits of a Roaring64Map. Internally iterates over the map of high-32-bit buckets and uses a 32-bit roaring iterator per bucket. Provides forward/backward iteration, lower_bound-like move, and standard comparison operators.

A 64-bit Roaring bitmap implemented as a map from high 32-bit words to 32-bit Roaring bitmaps containing the low 32-bit words. Provides construction from values/arrays/other bitmaps, set operations (union, intersection, difference, XOR), range adds/removes/flips, serialization (portable and custom), frozen views, rank/select, cardinality, subset checks, iteration, and copy-on-write support.
Type alias kept for backward compatibility; previously a separate forward iterator, now an alias of Roaring64MapSetBitBiDirectionalIterator.

Primary 32-bit Roaring bitmap handle. Owns a roaring_array_t of containers indexed by the high 16 bits, storing the set of uint32 values. Lifetime is managed by roaring_bitmap_create*/free, or by init/clear when stack-allocating.

Opaque per-bitmap context to accelerate repeated bulk add/contains operations by caching the last accessed container and position. Must be zero-initialized before first use and invalidated by any non-bulk modification.

Internal-state iterator for traversing values of a roaring_bitmap_t in ascending or descending order. Users should treat fields as opaque except current_value and has_value. Create via roaring_iterator_create or stack-allocate and initialize via roaring_iterator_init/roaring_iterator_init_last; free with roaring_uint32_iterator_free if heap-allocated.
Opaque 64-bit Roaring bitmap handle. The actual struct is not defined in this header; users manipulate it via the API. Lifetime is managed by roaring64_bitmap_create/free and friends.

Alias for a 64-bit unsigned integer used internally to represent or address leaf components of the 64-bit roaring bitmap. Serves primarily as a semantic typedef within bulk-context and related operations.
Opaque forward/backward iterator over elements of a roaring64 bitmap. The struct is not defined here; create, copy, advance/previous, and free via the provided iterator API.

Context object for accelerating repeated bulk add/remove/contains operations on a single roaring64 bitmap when values share the same high 48 bits. Must be zero-initialized before first use and invalidated by any non-bulk modification of the target bitmap.
Function-pointer typedef for an allocation function taking a size_t and returning a void* to a newly allocated block, or NULL on failure.
Function-pointer typedef for a reallocation function taking an existing pointer and a new size, returning a resized allocation pointer (or NULL on failure).
Function-pointer typedef for a zero-initializing allocation function taking element count and size, returning a pointer to cleared memory (or NULL).
Function-pointer typedef for a deallocation function taking a pointer previously allocated by the matching allocator and freeing it.

Function-pointer typedef for an aligned allocation function taking alignment and size (or size and alignment depending on convention; here order is (size, alignment) per declaration) and returning a pointer meeting the alignment requirement.
Function-pointer typedef for freeing memory allocated by the aligned allocator counterpart.

Structure holding a set of memory management function pointers used by the Roaring library. It allows overriding allocation, reallocation, calloc, free, and aligned allocation/free. Users can fill this struct and pass it to roaring_init_memory_hook to globally install custom memory hooks for the library. Field semantics mirror the standard C allocation API; aligned_* must be paired.

Contiguous 64-bit-word-backed dynamic bitset. The array field points to a buffer of 64-bit words; arraysize is the current number of words in use (size in words), and capacity is the allocated word capacity. Bits are addressed by global bit index. Operations include creation, resizing/growing, clearing/filling, set/get, shifts, set-bit iteration, and set algebra (union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference). Memory is managed manually; create with bitset_create or bitset_create_with_capacity and free with bitset_free.
Typedef alias for struct bitset_s representing the public bitset handle type. Same layout and semantics as struct bitset_s.
Function pointer type for iterating over set bits. The callback receives a set bit value and an opaque parameter and returns true to continue or false to stop. Used by bitset_for_each.
